key_insight: Under stronger upstream acoustic forcing, three distinct mesoscale flame regimes converge to a common oscillatory extinction-ignition state (O-FREI) marked by stronger forcing-frequency oscillations and reduced mean heat release.
engineering_relevance: The results help predict and control combustion stability in confined mesoscale devices such as portable power and micro-propulsion systems under acoustic disturbances.
method: Applied upstream acoustic forcing at the first harmonic of the combustor tube
Swept a broad range of pressure intensities across FREI, stable flame, and propagating flame regimes
Interpreted the dynamics with reduced-order mathematical models
evidence_signal: The abstract reports regime-wise observations across three flame states, showing low-intensity forcing causes frequency-locked oscillations, while higher forcing drives a shared O-FREI regime with lower mean heat release and reduced ignition-extinction Strouhal number.
watch_item: The conclusions are based on a specific confined mesoscale combustor and first-harmonic forcing conditions, so generalization to other geometries, fuels, or forcing spectra may be limited.
paper_title: Response of Confined Mesoscale Flames to Acoustic Forcing
